title: Make the review easier to follow
intro: The brief asks for a clearer review screen without losing capability. I focused on one task in Formbricks #8650: check a summary against the code, inspect the access guard, then return to the caller. The original already supports layers, summary jumps and viewed status.
rows: The filename, Mark viewed and Tools share one row. Display settings sit directly above the code. PR overview holds secondary destinations. This gives actions a clear scope, but adds a click to less frequent tools.
Moving across files can interrupt the review.

The file list uses one scrolling region with the layers. This file and Entire layer make the explanation’s scope explicit. Keeping both side panels costs code width; Focus restores that space without losing position.
One summary covers 82 lines and six points.

Each point links to its code. Inspect guard opens the related file; Return restores the caller’s selection and position. Full wording and Whole function stay available. Precise links can encourage tunnel vision, so they are starting points for inspection.
Reading and finishing are different decisions.

Opening a file marks nothing viewed. Mark viewed updates the file and count together, with Undo. Summary seen stays separate. The count covers seven included files; Submit review is disabled because this PR is merged.
tradeoff_title: What I chose to leave out
tradeoff: I kept one code pane. Putting caller and guard side by side would squeeze both at laptop width. The return action demonstrates continuity without another permanent panel. Added-file Split keeps its empty Before pane compact.
validation: The links, return path, focus, viewed state and Undo can be tried. These checks establish working behavior, not better comprehension. The design keeps 13 px code; larger type and modified-file Split still need developer testing.
scope: Pinned Formbricks #8650, commit 23cdac2 (out of date). Seven of 52 diffs are included. The original comparison capture is untouched. Links are manually mapped; layer-specific semantic diffs are not recreated.
next: Give developers the same task on both screens. Ask them to explain the guard and find a reason the summary could be incomplete. Compare missed branches, wrong turns and time spent finding their place. Faster navigation is only useful if they still understand the change.
